correctness.rationale: The asserted metric and sampling measure are independently reconstructed by unrolling a circular cone: two radial variables have density 2r and angular separation is uniform in [0, pi*kappa]. The squared-distance Hessian in radial variables is positive definite, hence global maximizers are exactly the listed square corners; no other maxima were overlooked. Uniform Taylor expansions localize subcritical rare events to two apex-rim neighborhoods (each contributes 4/alpha times a triangular moment), supercritical rare events to the single rim-rim corner (a 3-simplex of volume 1/(6a^2c)), and at the critical ratio contributions add. Explicit coefficient computations and numerical quadrature were checked, along with monotone coupling and moment normalization. The result is restricted to fixed 0<kappa<1 and omits base disk.

value.rationale: The endpoint law describes an extremal-intrinsic-geometry phenomenon on a canonical singular surface, including an exact change of maximizing pair geometry at a natural aspect ratio and additive competing contributions at the transition. Its coefficient is a meaningful invariant for rare near-diametral pairs and extreme-value sampling, not an arbitrary numeric slice. The cubic exponent is established for every nondegenerate cone, while the shape-dependent contact mechanism and critical amplitude require substantive geometric analysis.
